persistence_diagram.description: Birth-death pairs of topological features in a scalar field, computed by TTKPersistenceDiagram
persistence_diagram.interpretation: Each pair is a topological feature (a connected component, loop, or void) born and destroyed as an isovalue sweeps the field. Persistence is death minus birth: the vertical distance of a point above the diagonal. High-persistence pairs are robust features; low-persistence pairs near the diagonal are noise.

methods.min_saddle: Pairs a minimum with a 1-saddle; captures connected components of sublevel sets (0-dimensional homology)
methods.saddle_max: Pairs a 2-saddle with a maximum; captures voids / top-dimensional features
methods.saddle_saddle: 1-saddle to 2-saddle pairs; captures loops / tunnels (1-dimensional homology) in 3D

persistence_diagram.persistence_gap: A clear gap in the sorted persistence values separates signal from noise. Choosing a simplification threshold inside that gap removes noise while preserving genuine features.
persistence_diagram.design_relevance: The number of high-persistence pairs is the count of significant features in the field, independent of mesh resolution. Use it to decide a denoising threshold before extracting features.

critical_points.description: Points where the gradient of the scalar field vanishes, computed by TTKScalarFieldCriticalPoints
critical_points.interpretation: Critical points organize the field's structure. Their type is stored in the CriticalType array.

types.minima: CriticalType 0: local minima (basins / sources of sublevel-set components)
types.1_saddles: CriticalType 1: 1-saddles (merging of components, or loop creation)
types.2_saddles: CriticalType 2: 2-saddles (relevant in 3D; loop destruction / void creation)

critical_points.euler_relation: For a clean field the alternating count of critical points by index equals the Euler characteristic; large deviations indicate noise that simplification should remove.
critical_points.design_relevance: Counts of minima and maxima give the number of basins and peaks. In a CFD scalar field, maxima of pressure locate stagnation, minima locate suction cores.

morse_smale_complex.description: Segmentation of the domain into regions of uniform gradient flow, plus the separatrix skeleton, computed by TTKMorseSmaleComplex
morse_smale_complex.interpretation: The complex partitions the domain by which extrema the gradient flow connects. Output port 0 is the critical points, port 1 the 1-separatrices (the skeleton of integral lines between saddles and extrema), port 3 the segmentation.
morse_smale_complex.use: The 1-separatrices form a compact structural skeleton of the field. The segmentation labels each region by its ascending/descending manifold, giving a feature-based decomposition.
morse_smale_complex.design_relevance: Provides a structural decomposition of a field into its constituent features without thresholding, useful for comparing structure across cases or timesteps.

topological_simplification.description: Removal of low-persistence features below a threshold, computed by TTKTopologicalSimplificationByPersistence
topological_simplification.interpretation: Cancels critical-point pairs whose persistence is below the threshold, producing a denoised scalar field whose remaining topology reflects only significant features.
topological_simplification.threshold_guidance: Set the persistence threshold inside the persistence gap (see persistence_diagram). A relative threshold of a few percent of the field range is a common starting point; raise it to keep only the most prominent features.
topological_simplification.design_relevance: Denoising before feature extraction prevents spurious features (from mesh noise or solver residuals) from being reported as physical structures.

feature_identification.goal: Find the significant features in a scalar field and separate them from noise
feature_identification.rationale: The persistence diagram reveals the signal/noise gap; simplification removes noise at that gap; critical points on the simplified field are the genuine features.

structural_decomposition.goal: Decompose a field into its structural regions
structural_decomposition.rationale: The Morse-Smale complex segments the domain and extracts the separatrix skeleton without requiring a threshold.
